subject: physics
title: Charging, Discharging and the Time Constant
welcome_lead: Watch Q decay exponentially with time constant τ = RC.
meta_desc: A-Level Capacitance adventure on charging and discharging curves and time constant.
final_note: After 5τ the capacitor is essentially fully discharged (≈0.7%).

concepts.def: τ = RC, time for Q to fall to ~37%.

walkthroughs.body_html: Q(t) = Q₀ e^(−t/RC). At t = τ, Q = Q₀/e ≈ 0.37 Q₀. Current and voltage follow the same exponential. Larger RC means slower discharge.
Q(t) = Q_max (1 − e^(−t/RC)). Initially fast, then slows asymptotically. After 5τ, Q is within 0.7% of Q_max.
τ = R × C. With R in ohms and C in farads, τ is in seconds. Choose RC to set how fast your circuit responds — vital for filters and timers.
